key_insight: OpenCoF argues that video generation can be used as a new reasoning medium: instead of thinking only in text, a model can reason through temporally linked frames (Chain-of-Frame reasoning). The paper’s key idea is to better supervise and design video generators so they can express structured reasoning, not just produce realistic videos.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of dedicated supervision and model design for reasoning with video generation. Existing video generators are trained mostly on generic video datasets, which limits their ability to represent diverse logical steps across frames.
method: Introduces OpenCoF, a framework focused on learning reasoning through video generation.
Uses temporally connected frames as a reasoning pathway to model Chain-of-Frame (CoF) behavior.
Adds more diverse supervision and task-oriented design to improve a generator’s ability to express multi-step logical consequences in video form.
impact: This matters because it expands how AI systems can reason: not only by generating text explanations, but by producing structured visual sequences that reveal intermediate thought steps. For practitioners, this could improve interpretability, evaluation, and new multimodal reasoning applications.

paper_title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
paper_authors: Xinyan Chen, Ziyu Guo, Renrui Zhang, Dongzhi Jiang, Hongsheng Li
